title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on Prevention and Handling of Emergencies in Enforcement of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Issuance of the Notice on the Several Provisions on the Prevention and Handling of Enforcement Emergencies by People's Courts (Trial)

Fa Fa [2009] No. 50

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Provisions on the Prevention and Handling of Enforcement Emergencies by People's Courts (Trial) of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued to you for implementation in light of local conditions.

September 22, 2009

Several Provisions on the Prevention and Handling of Enforcement Emergencies by People's Courts (Trial)

In order to prevent and reduce the occurrence of enforcement emergencies, control, mitigate, and eliminate the social harm caused by enforcement emergencies, standardize the emergency response work for enforcement emergencies, protect the personal safety and property of enforcement personnel and other persons, and maintain social stability, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws, and in light of the actual work of enforcement.

Article 1. For the purposes of these Provisions, "enforcement emergencies" refer to incidents that occur suddenly during enforcement work, causing or potentially endangering the personal safety and property of enforcement personnel and other persons, seriously disrupting the order of enforcement work, and requiring emergency response measures to be taken. Such incidents include group petitions, self-harm by parties, gathering and blocking the enforcement site, resisting enforcement by violence or threats of violence, and similar events.

Article 2. According to factors such as the degree of harm and the scope of impact, enforcement emergencies are classified into four levels: especially major, major, relatively large, and general.

Especially major enforcement emergencies refer to incidents that seriously affect social stability, cause fatalities, or cause injuries or disabilities to three or more persons.

Except for especially major enforcement emergencies, the criteria for classification shall be formulated by each High People's Court according to the actual circumstances of its jurisdiction.

Article 3. High People's Courts shall strengthen guidance over the emergency response work for enforcement emergencies within their respective jurisdictions.

The emergency response work for enforcement emergencies shall be the responsibility of the enforcing court or the court handling the matter. People's courts at all levels shall establish an emergency response work institution headed by a court leader and establish relevant working mechanisms.

When an enforcement emergency occurs during enforcement in a different locality, the court at the place of occurrence must assist the enforcing court in carrying out on-site emergency response work.

Article 4. The work of responding to enforcement emergencies shall adhere to the principle of prevention first, combining prevention with emergency response. The emergency response to enforcement emergencies shall adhere to the principles of prioritizing personal safety and emphasizing social stability.

Article 5. People's courts at all levels shall formulate emergency response plans for enforcement emergencies. The enforcement emergency response plan shall include: organization and command, handling principles and procedures, prevention and resolution, emergency response measures, post-incident investigation and reporting, equipment and personnel support, and other matters.

Article 6. A full reporting system shall be implemented for enforcement emergencies before, during, and after the event. Enforcement personnel shall promptly report relevant circumstances to the enforcement emergency response work institution of their court.

When an enforcement emergency occurs during enforcement in a different locality, the court at the place of occurrence shall promptly report the relevant circumstances to the local Party committee and government.

Article 7. People's courts at all levels shall regularly conduct training on knowledge related to enforcement emergency response for enforcement emergency response personnel and enforcement personnel.

Article 8. When handling cases, enforcement personnel shall carefully study the overall enforcement strategy, pay attention to enforcement art and methods, actively work towards enforcement settlement, and prevent the occurrence of enforcement emergencies from the source.

Article 9. Enforcement personnel shall strengthen awareness of procedural fairness, strictly take compulsory enforcement measures in accordance with statutory enforcement procedures, standardize enforcement conduct, and prevent the escalation of conflicts that could lead to enforcement emergencies.

Article 10. Enforcement personnel must strictly comply with relevant regulations on enforcement work discipline, maintain integrity and self-discipline, and prevent the inducement of enforcement emergencies.

Article 11. Enforcement personnel shall conscientiously make preparations for compulsory enforcement and formulate targeted enforcement plans. Before taking compulsory measures, enforcement personnel shall comprehensively collect and study relevant information about the person subjected to enforcement, analyze the possibility of an enforcement emergency in conjunction with the social circumstances at the enforcement site, and study relevant emergency resolution measures.

Article 12. If, during the enforcement process, enforcement personnel discover signs of an enforcement emergency, they shall promptly report to the enforcement emergency response work institution. The enforcing court must activate the emergency response plan and take effective measures to fully resolve the crisis of the enforcement emergency.

Article 13. When conducting enforcement in a different locality, if enforcement personnel request assistance from the local court, the local court must arrange for a designated person to handle contact and coordination and make emergency preparations.

Article 14. An enforcement emergency response plan must be activated when any of the following circumstances occur:

(1) the number of petitioners related to enforcement matters is 15 or more;
(2) petitioners related to enforcement matters engage in unreasonable behavior, pestering leaders, storming government organs, or other conduct that seriously disrupts the working order of state organs;
(3) petitioners related to enforcement matters engage in self-harm;
(4) parties or related persons bring flammable, explosive articles, restricted knives, or other lethal weapons to petitions;
(5) parties or related persons gather and block the scene, potentially leading to loss of control of the enforcement site;
(6) parties or related persons use violence or threaten violence to resist enforcement at the enforcement site;
(7) other incidents that seriously affect social stability or endanger the safety of enforcement personnel.

Article 15. After an enforcement emergency occurs, enforcement personnel shall immediately report to the enforcement emergency response work institution. The person in charge of the emergency response work institution shall promptly activate the emergency response mechanism and take effective measures to prevent the situation from deteriorating. At the same time, coordinate with the public security organs to dispatch police promptly to control the scene and report the relevant circumstances to the Party committee and government.

Article 16. If an enforcement emergency causes casualties or property damage, enforcement emergency response personnel shall promptly coordinate with public security, health, fire, and other departments to organize rescue efforts, making every effort to mitigate harm and reduce losses.

Article 17. If continuing to take enforcement measures may lead to loss of control of the scene, incite violent incidents, or endanger personal safety, enforcement personnel shall immediately cease enforcement measures and promptly evacuate the enforcement site.

Article 18. When an enforcement emergency occurs during enforcement in a different locality, enforcement personnel shall promptly notify the court at the place of occurrence of the relevant circumstances, and the court at the place of occurrence shall actively assist in organizing and carrying out emergency response work. The court at the place of occurrence must immediately send personnel to the scene, simultaneously report to the local Party committee and government, coordinate with public security and other relevant departments to dispatch police to control the scene, and take effective measures to control the situation and prevent it from worsening.

Article 19. After an enforcement emergency occurs, the enforcing court must conduct a special investigation into the incident, prepare a written report, and submit it level by level to the High People's Court within five working days. For especially major enforcement emergencies, the High People's Court shall immediately organize an investigation and report in writing to the Supreme People's Court within three working days.

Article 20. The investigation report on an enforcement emergency shall include the following:

(1) the time, place, and course of the incident;
(2) the consequences of the incident, including casualties and property damage;
(3) the case(s) related to the incident;
(4) the preventive and handling measures taken by the relevant courts;
(5) analysis of the causes of the incident and summary of experience and lessons;
(6) determination of responsibility for the incident and handling; and
(7) other matters that need to be reported.

Article 21. If an enforcement emergency is caused by the fault of enforcement personnel, or if improper emergency response exacerbates the consequences of the incident, or if there is subsequent concealment, false reporting, or delayed reporting, the relevant personnel must be held accountable in accordance with relevant disciplinary measures.

Article 22. Where parties or related persons commit illegal or criminal acts during an enforcement emergency, the relevant court shall coordinate with public security, procuratorial, disciplinary inspection, and supervision departments to investigate and deal with them seriously in accordance with laws and disciplines.

Article 23. These Provisions shall take effect as of October 1, 2009.
